verdict.rationale: Reflect documents end-to-end encryption that the vendor cannot read: 'No one else can read them (not even us)' and 'Our servers can't read the contents of your notes'. Server storage, an iOS app and Windows support imply multi-device sync, but a dedicated official sync service is never explicitly documented. Separately, reflect.app text describes sync via iCloud Drive or Git, which is host-platform sync rather than an official service. A community report notes the encryption does not cover uploaded files and images, which limits its scope. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an official cross-device sync service, E2EE coverage of attachments and images, and independent hands-on corroboration of the encrypted sync.

support.subject: As a power-user, an official sync service keeps my notes updated across all my devices with end-to-end encryption the vendor can't read

citations.quote:
The contents of your notes are end-to-end  
encrypted. No one else can read them  
(not even us).
Your notes contents are end-to-end encrypted. Our servers can't read the contents of your notes, so we can't serve them up in the API.
End-to-end encryption keeps your notes secure.
